_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
LINKED grows when matched TUs become reachable in the port's linked call graph.
Actor methods and free functions both count. Enrollment alone does not increase
the count when the release build still dead-strips the unreachable object.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 861328718, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT13: tree clean, reconfigure with CONFIGURE DEPS 248/5, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10163, six proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate, a captured run showing both new game-init arms firing with the frame cross-check at 0 disagreements), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which counts every push of port/** and every pull request into the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge; the shipping branch takes landings only through such pull requests, with the count required by a branch rule (the 10163 landing merged as PR #2470 with both runs reading 10163). +7 over the previous stamp of 10163, +137 over the 2026-09-08 morning's 10033, +1049 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. The previous stamp's measuredAt read 2026-09-09; it was taken in the small hours of 2026-09-08 local time. Since the 10163 stamp: the test harness reads its frame number off the ROM's own frame state (data_0209d50c hosted for the first time, phase 6 run at the host loop's boundary, a default-on cross-check that exits on any disagreement: zero gain by design, the prerequisite for handing the frame to the ROM's loop), and two of the four refused arms of the ROM's game-init body now run as ROM code from the ROM's own main: the save-block clear (func_02013e64; the old refusal was stale, the grouped run had existed since an earlier lane) and the backup-device identify (func_02042f68 and five TUs behind it; the two ROM tables it reads were already hosted with ROM bytes). Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10163 -> 10170. Staged behind the next gate: the two wireless link-state readers (+2), the ROM's own archive-mount table and LoadArchive answering from it (+8), the comms fan-out running the ROM's narrow bodies and extending them for sixteen players (0 by design). Measured and open: the wireless chain is 260 byte-matched TUs behind one PXI channel and one shared buffer (+147 through rung W4, an ARM7-side stub); the ROM's game loop driving the frame is +72 behind two host moves the scouts ruled on; ten of eleven chain-gating exceptions compile clean under MSVC, blocked by unhosted data, not the toolchain.
